questions.q: In a Nigerian community, a child first learns attitudes towards elders, obedience and leadership mainly through interaction within the family. This process is an example of...
questions.explanation: Political socialisation is the process by which people acquire political attitudes and values, and the family is an early agent. Public opinion polling measures views; it does not describe a child learning attitudes.

questions.q: A newspaper publishes conflicting letters from readers about a proposed state health levy. This best illustrates the role of the mass media in...
questions.explanation: Newspapers provide a platform for debate and help shape and express public views. Conducting elections is the work of electoral bodies, while interpreting the constitution is primarily for the courts.

questions.q: Which of the following best shows that public opinion can be expressed through a non-electoral channel in Nigeria?
options: The National Assembly amending a law
Residents of a community signing a petition against the siting of a refuse dump
A court nullifying an unfair levy
Voters casting ballots in a local government election
questions.explanation: A petition is a direct, non-electoral way for citizens to express their views to government. Casting ballots belongs to elections, while amending laws and nullifying levies are actions of the legislature and courts respectively.

questions.q: The fundamental objectives and directive principles of state policy in the Nigerian Constitution are primarily intended to...
options: determine the procedure for electing the president
create immediately enforceable rights for every citizen
guide governments in promoting social justice and public welfare
define the powers of traditional rulers
questions.explanation: The directive principles set goals and policy guidelines for government, especially in promoting welfare and social justice. They are not mainly an election procedure or a definition of traditional rulers' powers; their enforceability is treated separately from ordinary fundamental rights.

questions.q: A District Officer issues an order, but residents obey only because they fear punishment by armed police. This situation best illustrates...
questions.explanation: Power is the ability to compel obedience, while authority is the accepted right to command. Obedience based only on fear of punishment shows the officer has power but lacks accepted authority.

questions.q: The essential difference between power and authority is that authority is...
options: the same thing as state sovereignty
accepted as the right to give commands
always based on the use of force
questions.explanation: Authority exists when those subject to a command regard the ruler or institution as having the right to issue it. Power may simply be the capacity to compel obedience, even by force, and it is not identical to sovereignty.

questions.q: The body empowered to conduct elections for the offices of President, Governor and members of the National Assembly in Nigeria is the...
questions.explanation: The Independent National Electoral Commission conducts federal and state elections, including those for the President, Governors and National Assembly. State independent electoral commissions handle local government council elections, while the other bodies perform different functions.

questions.q: In a two-round presidential election, a second ballot is held because...
options: new candidates are to be nominated after the first round
all candidates obtained exactly the same number of votes
no candidate secured the required majority in the first round
the electoral commission wishes to test the voting machines
questions.explanation: A run-off is held when no candidate meets the required threshold in the first round, so the leading candidates compete again. It is not held because of a tie among all candidates or to test machines.

questions.q: A major criticism of the first-past-the-post electoral system is that it...
options: can give a party a share of seats that is not proportional to its share of votes
requires a second ballot in every constituency
makes it impossible to keep the ballot secret
questions.explanation: First-past-the-post is criticised because the winning party often receives a seat bonus while parties with substantial votes may win few seats. The system still uses secret ballots and single-member constituencies and does not require a run-off in each constituency.

questions.q: Which of the following became Head of State after the death of General Murtala Mohammed in 1976?
questions.explanation: Murtala Mohammed was killed in the failed coup of February 1976, and Olusegun Obasanjo, then Chief of Staff, Supreme Headquarters, succeeded him. Buhari and Babangida later led military regimes, while Gowon had been overthrown in 1975.

questions.q: The military government that introduced the Structural Adjustment Programme (SAP) in 1986 was headed by
questions.explanation: SAP was introduced in 1986 under General Ibrahim Babangida, with measures such as trade liberalisation and naira devaluation. Buhari's regime preceded it, while Abacha came to power in 1993.

questions.q: The 1951 Macpherson Constitution is notable for establishing
options: the office of President of Nigeria
regional Houses of Assembly within a quasi-federal structure
a unitary system with no regional legislature
questions.explanation: The Macpherson Constitution provided for regional legislatures and a central legislature, moving Nigeria towards federal arrangements. It did not create the office of President or a one-party system.

questions.q: Which military ruler promulgated the 1999 Constitution of Nigeria?
questions.explanation: General Abdulsalami Abubakar promulgated the 1999 Constitution as part of the transition to civilian rule. Sani Abacha had died in 1998 before that constitution was issued.

questions.q: The Technical Aid Corps (TAC) scheme was established by Nigeria in 1987 mainly to
options: train Nigerian soldiers for peacekeeping in West Africa
provide skilled Nigerian professionals to needy African, Caribbean and Pacific countries
fund election campaigns in neighbouring states
promote the importation of foreign technology into Nigeria
questions.explanation: The TAC scheme was created to share Nigerian expertise with developing countries, especially in Africa, the Caribbean and the Pacific. It is not a military training programme or a fund for foreign elections.

questions.q: Nigeria's 1983 expulsion of many undocumented West African immigrants was directed mainly at nationals of
questions.explanation: The 1983 expulsion order, issued under the Shagari government, affected mostly Ghanaians and caused tension within ECOWAS. The other listed countries were not the main target of that exercise.

questions.q: A confederation is best described as a political union in which
options: the component states retain most sovereign powers and the central authority has limited powers
the central government can abolish the component states at will
the head of state is elected by the national parliament for life
all powers are concentrated in a single national legislature
questions.explanation: In a confederation, the central authority is weak and depends largely on the consent of the component states. The ability of a central government to abolish component units is more typical of a unitary arrangement, not a confederation.

questions.q: A system of government in which political power is held by a small group of people distinguished by wealth, family or military strength is called
questions.explanation: Oligarchy is rule by a small, privileged group, often based on wealth, family ties or military power. Democracy, by contrast, rests on popular participation and accountability.

questions.q: Which power of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) directly concerns the finances of registered political parties in Nigeria?
options: fixing the annual membership dues of political parties
registering the logos and symbols used by political parties
monitoring and auditing the accounts of registered political parties
conducting primaries to select candidates of political parties
questions.explanation: INEC is empowered to monitor and audit the finances and accounts of registered political parties, including their campaign funds. It may monitor party primaries and register party logos, but it does not conduct party primaries itself or fix the dues that parties charge their members.

questions.q: The Nigerian Medical Association, which seeks to influence health policy while promoting the interests of medical doctors, is best classified as a
questions.explanation: The Nigerian Medical Association is a professional association that uses pressure-group methods to influence government policy in the interest of its members and the medical profession. It does not contest elections as a political party, it is not primarily formed to promote a public cause on behalf of non-members, and it is not a statutory corporation created by government.

questions.q: The movement of a politician from one registered political party to another is described in Nigerian politics as
questions.explanation: Cross-carpeting refers to defection from one political party to another. Coalition building is an alliance between parties, party primaries are internal selection contests, and popular participation concerns citizens' involvement in politics.

questions.q: In the United Nations, which organ admits new member states on the recommendation of the Security Council?
questions.explanation: Under the UN Charter, the General Assembly admits new member states after the Security Council has recommended them. The Economic and Social Council coordinates economic and social issues, the International Court of Justice settles legal disputes, and the Trusteeship Council oversaw trust territories.

questions.q: The Peace and Security Council of the African Union was established mainly to
options: supervise national elections in member states
interpret the African Charter on Human and Peoples' Rights
prevent, manage and resolve conflicts on the continent
questions.explanation: The AU Peace and Security Council is a standing decision-making organ for the prevention, management and resolution of conflicts in Africa. Election supervision is generally handled by other AU or national bodies, public health coordination is not its primary mandate, and the African Court deals with Charter interpretation.

questions.q: The highest decision-making authority of the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) is the
options: Authority of Heads of State and Government
questions.explanation: The Authority of Heads of State and Government gives the final policy direction and takes major decisions for ECOWAS. The Community Court interprets community law, the Parliament is advisory, and the Council of Ministers handles specified ministerial matters below the Authority.

questions.q: Which of the following sources of revenue is constitutionally assigned to the Federal Government in Nigeria?
options: market tolls collected by local government councils
tenement rates on privately owned houses
personal income tax on residents of a state
questions.explanation: Customs and excise duties are within the fiscal powers of the Federal Government and are collected through its agencies. Personal income tax on residents is generally a state matter, while market tolls and tenement rates are local government sources of revenue.

questions.q: The derivation principle in Nigeria's revenue allocation is intended mainly to reward states that
options: contribute natural resources to the Federation Account
generate the lowest internally generated revenue
host the highest number of federal universities
questions.explanation: Derivation allocation gives special consideration to states from which natural resources, especially crude oil, are derived and paid into the Federation Account. Population size, presence of federal universities, and low internally generated revenue are not the rationale for derivation.

questions.topic: Separation of powers and checks and balances
questions.q: The President's refusal to assent to a bill passed by the National Assembly is an example of
questions.explanation: Withholding assent is an executive power that restrains the legislature by preventing a bill from automatically becoming law. Judicial review occurs when courts assess the constitutionality of acts, and federal character concerns equitable representation in public appointments.

questions.q: The Bauchi State House of Assembly invites the Commissioner for Education to explain the poor performance of public schools and considers whether to recommend his removal. This action best illustrates the legislature's power of
options: control of the civil service through promotion
questions.explanation: Inviting a commissioner to answer questions and considering action on his conduct is a form of legislative oversight, through which the legislature checks the executive. Judicial review belongs to the courts, while delegation of legislative authority occurs when the legislature gives law-making powers to another body.

questions.q: An order made by the Minister of Health under powers granted by an Act of the National Assembly to regulate private hospitals is an example of
questions.explanation: Delegated legislation is law made by a person or body, such as a minister, under authority conferred by an Act of the legislature. Judicial precedent is law developed through court decisions, and a constitutional amendment changes the constitution itself. The minister is exercising powers given by the Act, not vetoing it.

questions.q: A Ghanaian man has lived in Enugu for fifteen years, is of good character, satisfies the required tax and residence conditions, and takes the oath of allegiance. Through which method has he most likely acquired Nigerian citizenship?
questions.explanation: Naturalisation is the method by which a foreigner who satisfies statutory residence, character and other requirements, and takes the oath of allegiance, becomes a Nigerian citizen. Registration by marriage applies specifically where a foreign woman is married to a Nigerian citizen, a fact not stated here. Citizenship by birth depends on parentage or birth under constitutional conditions, not on long residence alone.

questions.q: The family, school, peer group and mass media are important agents through which citizens acquire political attitudes, beliefs and values. This process is called
questions.explanation: Political socialisation is the process through which individuals learn political norms, attitudes and behaviour from agents such as the family, school, peers and the media. Political apathy refers to lack of interest in politics, while public opinion polling measures views rather than forming them in this broad way. Civic naturalisation is not the term for learning political values.

questions.q: A constitution that shares governmental powers between a central authority and component units, with each level deriving its authority from the same document, is best described as
questions.explanation: A federal constitution divides legal authority between a central government and component units such as states, and the division is usually entrenched in the same supreme document. A unitary constitution concentrates power in the central government, while flexible and unwritten describe amendment procedure or form, not the division of powers.

questions.q: The principle which requires that governmental power be exercised according to definite rules and that rulers be accountable under the law is known as
questions.explanation: Constitutionalism is the doctrine that government power should be limited by law and exercised according to constitutional rules, with rulers accountable under those rules. Authoritarianism involves arbitrary or unchecked rule, while federalism is a territorial division of power and sovereignty is supreme authority. The emphasis on legal limits and accountability points to constitutionalism.

questions.q: A popular preacher in Lagos attracts large crowds, and many followers obey him because of his personal charm and extraordinary claims rather than because of law, office or inherited custom. According to Max Weber, this authority is best described as
questions.explanation: Charismatic authority rests on the personal qualities, appeal or perceived exceptional gifts of a leader. Traditional authority is based on inherited custom, while legal-rational authority rests on rules and the offices people occupy. The preacher's influence in the scenario arises from personal appeal, not from custom or formal office.

questions.q: The power of the Nigerian state to make and enforce laws over all persons and groups within its territory is best described as
questions.explanation: Internal sovereignty is the supreme authority of a state within its own territory, including the power to make and enforce laws over persons and groups there. External sovereignty refers to independence from control by other states in international relations, while legitimacy concerns acceptance of a government's right to rule. Delegated authority is limited power granted by a higher authority, not the supreme authority of the state.

questions.q: Which body is empowered by the Constitution of Nigeria to register political parties and monitor their finances?
questions.explanation: The Independent National Electoral Commission registers political parties and monitors their finances under the Nigerian Constitution. State electoral commissions conduct local government elections, while the Inter-Party Advisory Council is a consultative body for parties.

questions.q: In a local government election in Kaduna State, 80,000 valid votes were cast. A candidate scored 35% of the valid votes. How many votes did the candidate receive?
questions.explanation: 35% of 80,000 is calculated as 35/100 × 80,000 = 28,000 votes. Values such as 24,000 or 20,000 would correspond to different percentages.

questions.q: Which military administration in Nigeria launched the War Against Indiscipline?
questions.explanation: The War Against Indiscipline was launched in 1984 under the military administration of Muhammadu Buhari and Tunde Idiagbon. It was intended to promote orderliness, patriotism and civic responsibility.

questions.q: The creation of twelve states by the Gowon regime in 1967 was principally intended to
options: introduce a two-party system in the country
prepare Nigeria for immediate republican status
implement the recommendations of the Willink Commission on minorities
reduce the power of the regional governments and strengthen the federal centre
questions.explanation: The creation of twelve states replaced the old regions and reduced their political weight, thereby strengthening the federal government, especially during the civil crisis. It was not mainly aimed at creating a party system or implementing the Willink Commission's recommendations.

questions.q: Which feature best explains why Nigerian military governments often governed by decrees?
options: Decrees required approval by a two-thirds majority of the National Assembly
Decrees were made by the ruling military council without debate in an elected legislature
Decrees applied only during declared emergencies in the regions
Decrees became law only after a national referendum
questions.explanation: Military governments suspended or dissolved elected legislatures, so decrees were issued by military councils and took effect without parliamentary debate. The other descriptions wrongly suggest normal legislative checks or limited emergency application.

questions.q: Which statement best describes the constitutional significance of the Macpherson Constitution of 1951?
options: It expanded Nigerian participation in government through a more representative central legislature and ministerial appointments
It introduced a fully elected National Assembly with a Prime Minister as head of government
It entrenched a bill of rights and created the office of an executive President
It abolished the regional assemblies and placed all powers in a unitary central government
questions.explanation: The Macpherson Constitution widened Nigerian involvement in the central legislature and allowed elected representatives to take ministerial roles. It did not create a fully elected assembly, a Prime Minister, or an executive presidency.

questions.q: The 1960 Independence Constitution of Nigeria provided that the Head of State was
options: the Prime Minister, who combined the offices of Head of State and Head of Government
the Queen, represented in Nigeria by a Governor-General
an executive President elected directly by the people
a ceremonial President elected by the National Assembly
questions.explanation: Nigeria remained a constitutional monarchy in 1960, with the Queen as Head of State represented by a Governor-General, while the Prime Minister headed the government. The 1963 Republican Constitution later replaced the Queen with a Nigerian President.

questions.q: Nigeria's membership of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation has often generated debate within the country mainly because
options: membership requires Nigeria to withdraw from the Commonwealth
membership automatically makes Nigeria an Islamic state with Sharia as the supreme law
Nigeria is constitutionally a secular state, and critics fear that membership could weaken the principle of secularism
membership forbids Nigeria from conducting trade with non-Muslim countries
questions.explanation: The debate arises from Nigeria's religious plurality and constitutional secularism, with critics arguing that membership of a religiously identified organisation may affect the country's secular character. Membership does not automatically impose Sharia, require withdrawal from the Commonwealth, or prohibit trade with non-Muslim countries.

questions.q: A constitution vests executive power in a prime minister who is accountable to parliament, while a hereditary monarch performs largely ceremonial duties. This system of government is best described as
options: a parliamentary system under a constitutional monarchy
questions.explanation: In the arrangement described, the real executive comes from and is responsible to parliament, and the monarch is ceremonial, which is the hallmark of a constitutional monarchy with a parliamentary system. A presidential republic separates the executive from the legislature, while military oligarchy and confederation have clearly different structures.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes an oligarchy?
options: Government by a hereditary ruler who is above the law
Government shared between a central authority and regional units
Government by a small and privileged group
questions.explanation: An oligarchy is rule by a small group, often privileged by wealth, family or military position. Adult-citizen rule suggests democracy, absolute hereditary rule suggests absolute monarchy, and central-regional division suggests federalism.

questions.q: The document issued by a political party to the electorate during a campaign, stating the policies it will implement if elected, is called its
questions.explanation: A party manifesto states to voters what the party stands for and what it promises to do if elected. A constitution lays down organisational or state rules, a bill of rights protects liberties, and a calendar schedules events.

questions.q: Which of the following is a major function of an opposition party in a democracy?
options: Criticising government policies and presenting alternative programmes
questions.explanation: An opposition party checks the government by scrutinising its policies, exposing weaknesses and offering alternatives to the electorate. Election conduct and result announcement are the duty of the electoral body, interpretation belongs to the courts, and appointment of electoral commissioners is not the opposition's function.

questions.q: The United Nations specialised agency mainly responsible for global public health matters is the
options: United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization
questions.explanation: The World Health Organization coordinates international public health, including disease control and health standards. UNESCO deals mainly with education, science and culture; FAO with food and agriculture; and the ILO with labour standards.

questions.q: The African Union's Agenda 2063 is primarily aimed at achieving
options: the replacement of the United Nations in global peacekeeping
military annexation of disputed territories in Africa
long-term socio-economic transformation and integration of Africa
the immediate creation of a single African currency
questions.explanation: Agenda 2063 is the AU's long-term framework for inclusive growth, sustainable development and continental integration. It is not a plan for territorial annexation, immediate currency creation, or replacing the United Nations.

questions.q: Which of the following matters is placed on the concurrent legislative list in the Nigerian Constitution?
questions.explanation: Concurrent matters can be legislated on by both the federal and state governments, and public health is listed among them. Defence, currency and foreign affairs are exclusive federal matters.

questions.q: The body established in Nigeria to ensure that appointments into federal public institutions reflect the federal character principle is the
questions.explanation: The Federal Character Commission monitors and advises on the equitable distribution of posts and appointments among the states and other federating units. The Code of Conduct Bureau handles asset and conduct rules, the National Population Commission deals with population matters, and the Independent National Electoral Commission conducts elections.
